title: AZ-900 · Describe Azure identity, access, and security · Module assessment

questions.category: Describe Azure Architecture and Services > Describe Azure identity, access, and security
questions.question: Which statement best describes Microsoft Entra ID?

options.text: Protections for datacenter facilities and physical hardware
An authorization system that controls who can perform which actions on Azure resources and at what scope
Technology that synchronizes identities between on-premises Active Directory and Microsoft Entra ID
Microsoft cloud-based identity and access management service

questions.explanation: Microsoft Entra ID is Microsoft cloud-based identity and access management service.

questions.category: Describe Azure Architecture and Services > Describe Azure identity, access, and security
questions.question: In the context of this Microsoft Learn unit, what does Authentication refer to?

options.text: The cloud app or resource being accessed as a policy condition
Microsoft Entra capabilities for integrating and controlling access to cloud and on-premises applications
Verifying the identity of a person, service, or device before granting access
Using identity and device state with tools such as Intune and Conditional Access

questions.explanation: Authentication is verifying the identity of a person, service, or device before granting access.

questions.question: Which description correctly matches Single sign-on (SSO)?

options.text: The combination of a security principal, role definition, and scope

An encryption key whose lifecycle and access are controlled by the customer

questions.explanation: Single sign-on (SSO) is using one identity sign-in to access multiple trusted applications.

questions.question: Which of the following is the best definition of Application management?

options.text: An external user represented in a Microsoft Entra tenant for collaboration

Microsoft Entra capabilities for integrating and controlling access to cloud and on-premises applications
An encryption key whose lifecycle is managed by Microsoft for the service

questions.explanation: Application management is Microsoft Entra capabilities for integrating and controlling access to cloud and on-premises applications.

questions.question: What is the primary meaning of Device management in Azure fundamentals?

options.text: Replacing cryptographic keys periodically or according to security policy

questions.question: Select the TWO statements that are correct according to this unit.

options.text: Single sign-on (SSO): something the user knows, such as a password or PIN.
Authentication: verifying the identity of a person, service, or device before granting access.
Authentication: managed domain capabilities such as domain join, Group Policy, LDAP, Kerberos, and NTLM without customer-managed domain controllers.
Microsoft Entra ID: Microsoft Entra capabilities for integrating and controlling access to cloud and on-premises applications.
Microsoft Entra ID: Microsoft cloud-based identity and access management service.

questions.explanation: The correct pair is: Microsoft Entra ID — Microsoft cloud-based identity and access management service; and Authentication — verifying the identity of a person, service, or device before granting access.

questions.question: Which TWO statements accurately reflect the concepts covered in this unit?

options.text: Application management: requiring an additional authentication factor so a password alone is not sufficient.
Single sign-on (SSO): technology that synchronizes identities between on-premises Active Directory and Microsoft Entra ID.
Application management: something the user has, such as a phone or security key.
Application management: Microsoft Entra capabilities for integrating and controlling access to cloud and on-premises applications.
Single sign-on (SSO): using one identity sign-in to access multiple trusted applications.

questions.explanation: The correct pair is: Single sign-on (SSO) — using one identity sign-in to access multiple trusted applications; and Application management — Microsoft Entra capabilities for integrating and controlling access to cloud and on-premises applications.

questions.category: Describe Azure Architecture and Services > Describe Azure identity, access, and security
questions.question: Select TWO correct statements about the material in this Microsoft Learn unit.

options.text: Device management: something the user is, such as a fingerprint or facial biometric.
Microsoft Entra Connect: technology that synchronizes identities between on-premises Active Directory and Microsoft Entra ID.
Device management: identity synchronization from Microsoft Entra ID to Microsoft Entra Domain Services without syncing managed-domain-only objects back.
Device management: using identity and device state with tools such as Intune and Conditional Access.
Microsoft Entra Connect: something the user has, such as a phone or security key.

questions.explanation: The correct pair is: Device management — using identity and device state with tools such as Intune and Conditional Access; and Microsoft Entra Connect — technology that synchronizes identities between on-premises Active Directory and Microsoft Entra ID.

questions.category: Describe Azure Architecture and Services > Describe Azure identity, access, and security
questions.question: Which TWO statements are consistent with the unit content?

options.text: Microsoft Entra Domain Services: something the user knows, such as a password or PIN.
Microsoft Entra Domain Services: managed domain capabilities such as domain join, Group Policy, LDAP, Kerberos, and NTLM without customer-managed domain controllers.
Microsoft Entra Connect: a Microsoft passwordless authentication option using a device-bound credential and PIN or biometrics.
One-way managed-domain synchronization: identity synchronization from Microsoft Entra ID to Microsoft Entra Domain Services without syncing managed-domain-only objects back.
One-way managed-domain synchronization: a Microsoft passwordless authentication option using a device-bound credential and PIN or biometrics.

questions.explanation: The correct pair is: Microsoft Entra Domain Services — managed domain capabilities such as domain join, Group Policy, LDAP, Kerberos, and NTLM without customer-managed domain controllers; and One-way managed-domain synchronization — identity synchronization from Microsoft Entra ID to Microsoft Entra Domain Services without syncing managed-domain-only objects back.

questions.category: Describe Azure Architecture and Services > Describe Azure identity, access, and security
questions.question: Choose the TWO accurate statements.

options.text: Microsoft Entra Domain Services: an app that can support MFA and passwordless sign-in.
Multifactor authentication (MFA): something the user is, such as a fingerprint or facial biometric.
Knowledge factor: a hardware-based passwordless authentication option supported by Microsoft Entra ID.
Multifactor authentication (MFA): requiring an additional authentication factor so a password alone is not sufficient.
Knowledge factor: something the user knows, such as a password or PIN.

questions.explanation: The correct pair is: Multifactor authentication (MFA) — requiring an additional authentication factor so a password alone is not sufficient; and Knowledge factor — something the user knows, such as a password or PIN.
